Sordid flashbacks to Barceloneta clubs circa 2008. My Spanish was bad. I didn’t want to go clubbing. I wanted to do the same thing I did every night and play foosball at our local dive. My friends thought I needed to step away from the futboli table and onto the dance floor to experience a bit of Aughts euro culture. To show my disdain i ordered the cheapest whiskey the club had, with coke and ice. Or so I thought. I confused “barato” with “caro” and instead was the a**hole in a navy sweatsuit unknowingly ordering Johnny blue. I stepped in just in time to say to the bartender “sin hielo y cola, por favor!” when I realized what was happening. I drank my vastly overpriced, misanthropic whiskey in self-disgusted silence while my friends danced to songs exactly like this. I never returned to the clubs, there or anywhere else—except for an ill-fated tryst in Vieques years later where I split my pants—but you bet your culata I made lifelong friends in that little foosball bar. Zero points.

The song's frank discussion of birth control, something that was considered risqué subject matter at the time (especially in country music), led to a number of country radio stations refusing to play it. 1950s George Bob Siggins leaves rural Nebraska for Harvard via train. In Cambridge he studies molecular neuroscience but falls into the folk scene. Early mainstay at Club 47 (Passim) while completing his PhD. I remember seeing love letters from Ronstadt and EmmyLou and a photo of him and Dylan on a motorcycle. To me he was a scientist and a surfer and the best family friend. I didn't know about his past with music, which was also a present, always playing. My parents met him in the late 70s in SD when he was a postdoc in the same lab as my dad. GB redefined how the scientific community thought about addiction on the neurotransmitter level. A truly world-class scientist. He loved wine and had a trap-door cellar in his home in Del Mar. His children are wonderful humans. He passed in 24 at 85 and John Leventhal played a song that I'll never forget. He didn't love this album title; wanted it to be beatles bluegrass. This song taught me to love bluegrass. Much more 2 share in >1K characters
